text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- State oil company NNPC retreats from new policy that oil products marketers should pay cash before lifting petroleum products after this caused fuel shortages in Nigeria.
- Nigeria earned $17 million last year from export of polyethylene and polypropylene from Eleme Petrochemical Plant in the midwestern Delta state.
- Military adminstrator of the oil-producing state of Bayelsa Navy Captain Oladipo Philips was at the weekend flown to Germany for treatment for an undisclosed illness.
- Airline operators and government to meet in the capital Abuja on Tuesday to agree on new fares for domestic flights.
- Major capital market operators may be required by the authorities to raise their capital base by 300 percent, market sources say.
- State-run Nigerian Telecommunications Ltd recorded 15 billion naira shortfall in revenue in 1996 from its target of 31 billion naira for the year, industry sources say.
- Central Bank withdraws 8.7 billion naira from circulation through sale of treasury bonds.
- Trade fair complex in northern Kaduna city refurbished at cost of 1.25 billion naira for African trade fair due to open there at the end of March, an official says.
- Investors inject 173 million naira in breweries by buying 11.6 million shares in the sector on the Nigerian stock market last week.

- There are indications that former vice president Augustus Aikhomu, interior minister Baba Gana Kingibe and ambassador to Israel O. Olisemeka are among those being considered for posting to London as Nigeria's high commissioner to Britain.
- Central bank may re-introduce treasury certificates to curb excess liquidity, banking sources say.
- Fuel tanker drivers in Warri, home city of detained former leader of oil workers' union NUPENG, Frank Kokori, reject move to impose a levy on them to raise funds for Kokori's family.
